notes.title: August Round-Up! 🗺️
notes.content:
Hi Seedlings! 


I hope everyone had a great summer! These past few months have been incredibly for us with game developement. With the new areas coming together nicely, we figured this monthly round-up is a good time to give everyone an early preview!


New Areas!
ICYMI, last month we’ve shared some blurred teasers of our new maps, and this time we are excited to show them in full HD. (We’d have loved to do it in 4K but alas, upload size limit…)

 [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/fcdecfbace67be3250a26895f4fce5f3574d73dc.png"]

The Brazen Plains is a vast open area surrounded by mountains. Numerous creatures roam the plains, and the surrounding mountains have all the nooks and crannies (and a MASSIVE lake) for you to explore.

 [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/3cf5009614014008af8eeb00eab15006ad80c3d3.png"]

The Volcano is a blazing inferno filled with environmental hazards and dangerous creatures. Mind your steps, and don't step on the lava!

 

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/089601068f03033177538271d895ceee23b23bf5.png"]

Here’s another new area not included in last month’s screenshots – the Scrapshire Village. Populated by quirky characters (you might spot some speech bubbles in the backdrop), you can take on many fun challenges for bountiful rewards!

 

Aside from the maps, we’ve been working on new body parts for the full game. Below is a screenshot of some of them combined on a single creature. What creatures do you think they belong to? Take a guess, and we’ll talk about them in the next monthly blog!



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/242ad3c1d88fbdf2106996b9a445a89b12bd664c.png"]


Community Creations
Before we go, let's check out what bizarre life forms our community made in the last month. We’ve received a number of awesome submissions from our Discord member Deathclawstudios. Here are some of their cool designs!



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/b87473ebbb942248582d065e956ccf162b80a4b0.png"]

This dragonfly has some impressive stats: over 200 stamina! That looks more than enough to soar across any map with ease!


[carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/b36b007e87af1cb117bd6b15e7fededf2581aaf2.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/85e16db5e4ecd64cd881a30a1be169a709299339.png"][/carousel]
They also recreated other IRL animals like a vulture and a fly with tools available in the demo. Look at the vulture spreading its massive wings!



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/f39e1dbad1bc19049411e797844689434396e56a.png"]



While this is all for this blog post, we'll be sharing more about the full game in the upcoming round-ups! Be sure to follow us on our socials and check back in next month!



Twitter YouTube TikTok

notes.title: July Round-Up! 🗺️
notes.content:
Hi Seedlings! 


Over May and June, we've implemented various updates to polish the demo in both gameplay and visuals. After consolidating the existing content in our demo, we feel it is time to start working on the next steps of Strange Seed. Here's a little (blurry) teaser on a couple of the new maps that we've been making!


New Areas Sneak Peek🖼️[carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/94e3790e34d40a68b7f858294cebb571252754b7.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/262c2987ed95c9679e8f1b29fcb850fae8cbd053.png"][/carousel]
The screenshots here only show 2 of the several new areas that we've been preparing for the full game. We want to make sure each of them will offer a different experience so we've been putting a lot of thought into laying down a large variety of puzzles, missions and enemies to make every map feel intriguing and distinct. Be ready for new encounters and new challenges!



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/0d6cdbf5da1596e885b4d2e70397e6eaf2b6f055.png"]

New Area, New NPCs




An Indie Games Celebration! 🌏
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/f6bc214eb80c877f6ec8735581afeba0984d2427.png"]

Going into August, Strange Seed will be make an appearance at another exciting Steam event: the East Asia Indie Games Celebration (Aug 5-19). We are very grateful for being accepted to this event in recognition of our Asian team members' contribution to this evolutionary RPG. Check out their absolutely massive collection of awesome indie games from East Asia!


Community Creations🎨
Now it's time to look at our community's creative designs again. As always, our players came up with some bizarre rather critters. Here are a couple designs by orinz:



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/ff83a021a1a6f1783bfa9f68c1cf84c26ef36413.jpg"]A colorful cryptid, this creature not only has insect body parts, but also makes use of the cyborg tail to repel enemies with lethal stings!



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/5a9ebf2e01ae76a9075c19c6f2971101e580def7.jpg"]A giant, enemy spider. For a cosmetic creature it is surprisingly capable in combat, with both offensive and defensive abilities alongside a solid stat line.



Thank you for joining us for this community round-up. More exciting news is coming soon, so keep a lookout on our socials for more updates!



Twitter YouTube TikTok

notes.title: June Round-Up! 🍖
notes.content:
Greetings seedlings! 


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/0a67f9cbfe4d60c156ae6f1cfbccc253728cba8f.png"]The July heat is coming in full swing. Our Pink Blob already took out its sunglasses to enjoy the summer beach. Our devs, though, decided to stay out of the scorching sun to work on the next batch of update instead. Here’s what we have for this monthly round-up!  


More Visual Updates!
You might have noticed our game looks a little different from before – that’s because we sneaked in another visual update in June! A couple highlights of the changes:



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/59d589c19b8235b38e4765af0010943538e8a733.gif"]

In the evolution panel, body part changes now trigger an animation to add more character and energy to our little Pink Blob (plus it is a nice visual indicator of body part changes).



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/154357bad77e4cf8164acd339e4057093c0eb86f.png"]

The nest UI now recolors depending on which area you are in, to give your nest a more thematic look.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/9029f2ad9ac19e818e51243817561a129dfad426.png"]

There are also changes to visuals including particles and colors in the demo. You can see more details (and all our past updates) on our Steam update thread.


Canadian Games Sale
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/bf775e80aece0c648da127ec9454fef2d6f92b80.jpg"]

Strange Seed will soon take part in the Canadian Games Sale! From July 1 to July 7, over 300 games from the land of maple, including us, will be on display! Check out all the promising upcoming games and exciting released titles here.


Community Creations
After covering all the monthly news, it’s time to share all the bizarre life forms designed by our creative community!



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/f74bb79a8127096be88fb19b22e157f49caa0cea.png"]

Our Discord member silly lil goober made a creature so fast it might have broken the chicken head part when it goes zoom (But this is too funny so I think we’re just going to leave it. It’s a [strike]bug[/strike] feature.)



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/df274f6d5efcb40985eb0094bf8be4b0aca125b8.jpg"]A creepy creation by Gear. Why does it look like it has an explosive temper?



And that's all we've got for this monthly round-up! Join our Discord server to talk about Strange Seed and share your own peculiar creature designs! Follow our Twitter, YouTube and TikTok for the latest news of Strange Seed!

notes.title: May Round-Up! 🍖
notes.content:
Welcome back seedlings! 

Have you noticed Strange Seed is a bit different from how it was two months ago? That's right, we've introduced multiple updates to the game over the last two months! Let's jump right in and see what's new!


Sneaky Updates
Throughout April and May, we’ve been sneaking in an array of control optimizations, control bug fixes, new content and more to flesh out the demo! Here are a couple of highlights: 
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/2c6e19cf9403acc3d503e12eb24f595651e702d4.png"]Pink blob can now glide with beetle wings!

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/b4e733a375cc91352aff0b680d38dc2630b1e27d.png"]Certain NPCs now have tombstones, and some can be revived for a cost...



Scroll down to the bottom of this blog post for the full list of changes.  
Steam Events
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/76695c647df7141a4812bf21ad4e5880c707c287.png"]You can also find our pink blob in multiple events in May. We started the month with Indie Assemble, a global indie game festival organized by Excaliber. With 600 development studios participating, this event showcased over 1,000 released titles and upcoming games from May 5 to May 11.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/dacd886f59d65db12b9e2fbb5678dae019b7fe5c.png"]We also collect creatures… with our bellies. Right after Indie Assemble, from May 12 to May 19, we took part in the Creature Collector Fest alongside many other titles that feature unique and bizarre creatures!


Strange Creatures by Our Fans
Before we wrap up today’s blog post, let’s check out what peculiar life forms our community came up with during May!

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/bbed958c4d72ce92fd2e234a7425f34fd703ec74.jpg"]We don’t currently have frogs in the Strange Seed but that doesn’t seem to stop our players from making their own! Here is an attempt by Chonk to recreate the amphibian in the game. There’s even a tadpole stage being shared on the Discord channel!

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/fe2c96e5c65a5ba934cab6eef53bff7ad03cbf75.png"]This gentleman named Scrunkly is the creation of Grimluck the Golem. Not sure if this is intentional but the stag beetle mandibles do resemble a moustache, and pairs quite well with the hat.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/d2d09e53f0fdd4893c7d9c18cfc6f3c913ba0e80.jpg"]And finally, we have the Wiggler from Chile Dawg, a creature that's 90% neck. If you don't want to drown, just evolve your neck longer than the water level.

If you're interested in sharing your own creature creations, join our Discord server!

That's all for May. See you all next month, and follow us on Twitter, YouTube and TikTok for all the latest news (and memes) of Strange Seed!




April 5 & April 10 updates:
 Hey! Are you a murder hobo!? Well guess what, now you can kill EVERYTHING!


 ... as a result, a small number of previously unavailable creature parts can now be found


 Tombstones: some unique enemies leave a tombstone behind; few of these allow you to revive the enemy (for a price)


 Faster recovery after attacks, so now you can quickly use two separate attacks, or more easily attack then block


 More fixes to prevent compost balls from getting stuck on their way to the pit


 Fixed bug causing slow startup time for the game from Steam


 New / different sound when you die


 Fixed missing Playstation controller icon in UIs


 Fixed tombstone issues (not loading when they should, loading when they shouldn't)


 Fixed jump animation not triggering sometimes


 Added a new Arms part for killing Rosa


 Fixed the dark grey ground splotch that appeared after dying


 Fixed the weird shimmer that appeared on objects sometimes (specular aliasing)


 Fixed wings issues (t-posing during attack, giant size when using geoduck head)




May 12 & May 14 updates:
 No more snake minigame in DNA recombination -- snake haters rejoice!


 ... but, DNA recombination can now lose Mystery Liquid (we'll add a new source of it soon)


 Glide ability added, for all fly/glide parts hold down jump to transition to gliding


 Base climb angle increased (so it's easier to climb now)


 Improved animation transitions during attacks


 Some graphical updates in various areas (hopefully improvements)


 Better camera tracking for fast-moving creatures (especially flying / falling ones)


 Better collider positioning for bipedal / vertical creatures


 Camera auto-zoom out for bigger creatures


 Geoduck neck no longer bumps everything and anything (but as a result, it will clip into walls freely)


 Updated transition animation when moving between scenes


 Drowning bar now depletes instead of fills


 Tombstone for Rosa now gives out her arms if you missed them


 Bug fix: player controls no longer lock up when using jump + attack while being attacked


 Bug fix: player controls no longer lock up when shooting ranged attacks into the void


 New creature shrine available somewhere in Honey Cliffs


 Fixed sun in cliffs and beach passing through objects


 Fixed Rosa's tombstone position


 Fixed Rosa bossfight not doing any damage to player (oops)


 You can now murder the sweet, innocent race organizer

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/3529bf71a988be54b1e4e151077c9114595ff547.png

notes.title: 2024 Recap!
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/2f1d41b2b2fca8cbf22a003d239800f201bb046c.png

2024 is ending and this year we have accomplished A LOT with Strange Seed. Playtest, demo release, updates, and even finding ourselves a publisher! Let’s do a quick recap of the year!

Demo Release and Updates!
On September 26, 2024, the Strange Seed demo went online. A massive thanks to our amazing playtester group. We’ve made many substantial changes to the game based on all the feedback in the playtest, with new content, new features, bug fixes, more bug fixes, optimizations, and… did I mention bug fixes? 

Of course, a demo is just the beginning, and we are continuously updating the game with new feedback coming in every day (a shoutout to everyone who checked out our demo and gave us even more helpful feedback). In November, we had 2 demo build updates which introduced a myriad of optimizations in gameplay, UI and performance, as well as more bug fixes and new content.

If you run into any new issues in Strange Seed, do let us know via the in-game feedback form or our Discord feedback channel so we can get it fixed asap!
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/46b58077d709d9c76fa3734cb3f4489ead617dac.png


New Publisher
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44255762/5bb145bd57d7f6776fab10205cf37bab49724a70.png

We are really happy to join up with Slug Disco as our publisher this year. With their support, we are taking more time to polish Strange Seed and evolve it a little more before going into a full launch. Here’s a sizzle reel on their YouTube channel and we are in there too!

[previewyoutube=fWK_-d_wlvc;full][/previewyoutube]
Plans for 2025
We are currently aiming for a 2025 release, as we are looking to expand the game with more creature parts, more abilities and more areas. We will be looking for playtesters around early 2025 for areas not included in the demo version. If you want to get a sneak peek of our content early, join our Discord to get updates on our playtest!

We hope everyone had an awesome 2024 and is enjoying Strange Seed’s demo. We are super grateful for such a dedicated and supportive community to our game and our game would not be the same without all your help. Every demo download, every wishlist and every piece of feedback helps our little pink blob evolve into something better. 

With 2025 closing in, there’s more content around the corner so please look forward to our new evolutions! Make sure you follow us on Twitter, YouTube and TikTok as well for the latest Strange Seed news (and memes)!

notes.title: Announcing our publisher and 2025 release
notes.content:
Strange Seed has found a publisher! We're happy to announce that we've joined up with Slug Disco.

In case you don't know Slug Disco, they're actually a developer too -- they make Empires of the Undergrowth, the world's best strategy game about ants. They're also the publisher of Adapt, a Spore successor. You can probably guess why we thought they're a good match.

What's changing?
We'll take more time to polish Strange Seed. Originally we were rushing to launch and didn't have the funds needed to make the game its best. With Slug Disco's assistance and advice, we'll push that launch date back several months into 2025 and spend the extra time making the game great(er).

As far as the game's core mechanics, we won't be making any drastic changes from what you can see in the demo. The focus is on more creature parts, more abilities and more areas.

Want to test out the full game early?

In early 2025, we'll be looking for playtesters to try out some of the areas that aren't included in the demo. 

If you're interested, join up to our Discord so that you can see our announcement when we're signing up testers.

We hope you're enjoying Strange Seed, and that we'll see you in the future!
- the Chronicle Games team

notes.title: Demo launch date: Sept 26

Our demo will be going live on September 26. Here’s a link to the demo page:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3224660/Strange_Seed_Demo/

 New Cliffs area with two quests

But if you want to try out an interesting, quirky RPG, look for the button directly above this post that says “Request Access”. Then click it!

notes.title: Early 2024 dev log: environments, quests and more!
notes.content:
We’re well into the phase where the game starts to feel pretty cohesive. Here’s our new “forest hallway” environment that I haven’t yet added to the Steam screenshots:

https://steamuserimages-a.akamaihd.net/ugc/2497884302569691828/EF323062127BD66F4B74CED396E22EAC4342E9F1/?imw=1024&imh=664&ima=fit&impolicy=Letterbox&imcolor=%23000000&letterbox=true 

Some of the tasks that went into making our new environments included:

 A fully featured lighting and shadow system
 New shaders for all vegetation and environment objects
 Completing the climbing system
 A bunch of new vegetation models made in Speedtree

The challenge is getting these environments to work well on lower-end computers. 

I’m testing on my old Nvidia 1060 laptop and they’re stable at >30 FPS; I wonder if anyone with a lower end rig will be wanting to play? Luckily there is still some low-hanging fruit left for optimization.

The quest system
The other major feature we’re working on polishing right now is a quest system. After some back and forth about how to code the quests, we settled on a pretty powerful system using a visual scripting system, via a 3rd party package. 

We've successfully put together a quest that involves grabbing a hat for the Queen Ant. Maybe you'll get to wear the hat afterward...?

Finally, a grab bag of other things we’ve been working on:

 Set up permanently flying creatures (like bees)
 Implemented a wrapper scene and sub-scene switcher that should both ease our workflow and make the game more stable
 Investigated and fixed various weird results from unexpected part combos
 Added a “treasure chest” feature tied to completing enemy encounters

Is a demo ever coming? Well, the game is nearly ready for it! … but, we kept putting off final polish on the movement system. Early playtesting surfaced a few bugs in that area, so we’re spending time stomping those out before doing a fully public demo. 

I think we’ll be ready in a couple months (probably after Steam Next Fest, because releasing a demo in that time frame without being in the Fest is a bad idea). That said, if you want in on pre-public playtesting, DM me or join the Discord.

That’s all for today, thank you for reading and following Strange Seed!

notes.title: October dev log: combat lock-on, controllers, insects!
notes.content:
October was a very productive month for us! Strange Seed is beginning to feel very “playable”, even though there’s much work left to be done.

Combat lock-on
Combat feels completely different with this change: locking-on to enemies. This includes an auto-rotate to attack and auto camera rotation while moving around.

New creatures: ant and bee
https://steamuserimages-a.akamaihd.net/ugc/2191624307495692711/350176CE2870EF3A72046E5C08CBC1C5C42E2C8E/?imw=5000&imh=5000&ima=fit&impolicy=Letterbox&imcolor=%23000000&letterbox=false 😀

Controllers (of all types!) enabled
Pretty much everything should work now! I’m a controller-first guy and being able to constantly test Strange Seed using a controller is a huge, positive change for me.

… actually, I haven’t tried playing with a joystick or rhythm game accessory yet, so I can’t claim “everything” 😅 Let’s just say, any typical game controller.

Controller: ranged attack hold to aim
Once we had the controller in, we realized that ranged attacks need a special control scheme when there’s no mouse. With a mouse, you just click wherever you want to attack. With the controller, hold L1 and move the joystick to position the landing zone. (This makes me want to play Valkyria Chronicles again…)

Final word
Originally I thought we’d have a rough demo out by now, but the plan was to have very incomplete combat mechanics. When it came down to it, combat felt so central to the game that we needed to work on polishing it before the demo.

So that’s what we’re doing right now — in November, we’ll be running some private playtests of combat in greybox levels, ensuring that our attack timing, movement scheme, encounter design and so forth is really solid.

Thanks for reading!

notes.title: September dev log: adding skin swapping
notes.content:
This month we added a material and color user interface. Every creature has its own skin, and now that skin can be applied to others and recolored. Here's a quick video:

[previewyoutube=RTE93i7wFLM;full][/previewyoutube]

… I have a personal compulsion to make everything neon, but normal colors work just fine too.

This was pretty complex to set up because of all the small details: tying into our evolve system; making decisions for sub-parts and special cases; and accounting for a variety of shaders. All that said, the feature was completed within the allotted time (there are still future improvements to make, of course).

Other things we completed this month:

 New creatures: tortoise and snake
 Performance testing and work within scenes to improve FPS for low-end devices
 Some dance animations (just for fun… for now)
 Continued improvements on AI movement via the NavMesh
 Started on ambient enviro sounds, bugfixes for existing creature sounds

Headed into October, we’re working on controller implementation, combat polish, and some new environments. By the end of the month, we'll also revamp our Steam store page with a bunch of new assets -- exciting!

Thanks for reading!

notes.title: August devlog: sloggin' the swamp
notes.content:
Happy Labor Day everyone! In August we began kicking the tires on some existing systems, making sure the foundation is solid going into the second half of developing Strange Seed.

Here are some of the major tasks we completed:

 New player/enemy creatures: pig and failed evolve slimes (enemy only)

https://i.imgur.com/laLBkie.png

 Added NavMesh-based enemy AI / navigation and more AI behaviors
 Improved the look and timing of ranged and area attacks
 Exhaustively investigated various potential refactorings to our ground collision system
 Completely revised and replaced our evolution UI and HUD styling
 Studied performance: on most of our dev machines, the game runs at 60fps or well above that, but on a couple older laptops, it’s experiencing drops under 30fps; this appears to be mainly an issue with draw calls, which means it’s very solvable by offering alternate performance options for lower-end machines
 Evaluated and tested various occlusion and frustrum culling methods to get higher FPS across all devices

Overall I’m pretty happy with the results of our refactoring and reevaluation of the core systems. In early August I found myself feeling semi-panicked about the quality of collisions in the game — not based so much on anything that was actually going wrong, but more on what might go wrong in the future. (Hey, I just get nervous sometimes, alright!?)

As a result, I got together with my engineer Felix and we evaluated a bunch of potential options. First, for the ground collisions, we considered replacing an existing torso-based system with a per-foot system, which would also change up how we did walk and run animations.

In the end we got together with our artist, Jhulian, and did a team evaluation of the old system versus the new idea. And as a group we decided… our existing system is actually the best option! This might sound like a story that goes nowhere (hah) but for me, it was a great moment; it means we’re on the right track.

We actually did end up changing the attack collision system, to use primitive colliders (mainly capsules and spheres) to register combat hits. That’s a fairly standard system for 3d games and for us, it worked perfectly from the first test.

https://i.imgur.com/zCRCEbm.png

As a last word, when I was writing this post I realized that a comic from a book on gamedev (by Matt Hackett) described this month perfectly:

https://pbs.twimg.com/media/FzrWUrSagAA_TvF?format=jpg&name=4096x4096

We clearly spent August in the Slog Swamp — except for Jhulian, who spent half his time on Content Mountain. Our team has been working together for years now with various finished projects under our belts, so the Swamp isn’t nearly as uncomfortable as it used to be. It’s actually a fairly satisfying place, when you manage to make some progress.

See you next month!

notes.title: July development log: perfecting the creature
notes.content:
This month we made a ton of progress on the fine details of the creature system — including special poses like climbing, tweaking odd size and part combinations, fixing physics issues, and improving combat.

Going into August, we’ll continue making some improvements to the character rig and ground collision. Polishing these was initially planned for later; however, to ensure that we deliver a great demo, we’ve moved them up.

Finished in July:

 New creatures: geoduck and monkey (both ranged attackers)
 Special setup for ranged attacks: rules around attacking near / far, attacking slanted surfaces like cliffs, and projectile trails
 Switched up how we detect hits to be much more accurate
 Fixed wing rotation to avoid clipping through torso
 New attack VFX for all creatures (we switched from animations to a Trail Renderer)
 Allowed arms or legs to ragdoll if they can’t reach the ground… by the way, this is hilarious:
 Enemies: Fixed various navigation and behavior errors
 Enemies: No more insta-aggroing the entire zone, and reset properly on player death
 Enemies: Added combat music! Thanks to Donahue Industries for that.
 Player creature: Added a summed stats panel to the evolve UI
 Player creature: Fixed how some parts display in the UI
 Player creature: Drowning when underwater


Coming up in August (partial list):

 Updates to rig and collision (already mentioned above)
 Complete UI overhaul to replace our initial placeholders
 Nailing down combat stats for initial creatures and enemies
 Improving on ranged enemy attacks (melee comes first in this game, but ranged weapons do exist!)


See you for the next update!

notes.title: Game announce FAQ: doing justice to creature evolution!
notes.content:
Hi there! We’re a team of 3 indie devs — Chris (me), Jhulian and Felix — that believes the idea of creature evolution has never gotten the respect it deserves.

For me, the best game ever in the genre is E.V.O.: Search for Eden, an old SNES game. I highly recommend that everyone who enjoys classic games go play it. But the name that most people recognize is Spore.

Unfortunately, Spore bombed hard on release and that was mostly the end of the genre.

So indies need to save the day! Can we? Well, we’re trying. Here’s a FAQ about us.

Why build it?
Because creature evolution could be f%#ing amazing...

...but post-Spore, every other big company has avoided it like the plague.

What is it?
Strange Seed is an RPG, not a simulator! We want evolves to actually do something. Both make numbers bigger (an RPG classic) and function uniquely in the game world, adding a Metroidvania-style component to world traversal. For instance:

 Wings give you real flight abilities
 Tiny creatures can crawl into holes
 A big head with horns can break down barriers
 Predator eyes can see in the dark or infrared
 Chunky claws can dig
 A long neck or tongue can reach things

But I want a simulation game!
Great! There are some amazing evolution simulator games either in development or out already. Adapt and Elysian Eclipse are in the works. Thrive, Niche and The Sapling are out on Steam. If you’re developing or know another feel free to do some self-promo and comment it, or say hi.

Uh, can we go back to talking about Strange Seed now?

Fine… if it’s an RPG, what game is it most like?
Tough question, and it’s something we think about constantly! Based on these points:

 An inventory and treasure collection mechanics
 Mostly melee-range combat
 Some, but not a lot, of dialogue

The answer would be… Dark Souls? But there aren’t a ton of melee 3D RPGs, of which vanishingly few use non-humanoid characters, so it’s a really imperfect comparison. We’re also FFXIV enjoyers over here, and you’ll see hints of that in the combat system.

What about the creature customization, can I build anything I want?
We chose a different system that we think has its own unique strengths.

Spore and most 3D evolution simulators make use of parts that are sometimes called “metaballs”. This is basically like a blob of Play-Doh that needs to be stretched and shaped. Then fully procedural animations (i.e. just based on math) take care of stuff like walking and attacking. It’s an amazing innovation that results in interestingly weird looking creatures. BUT, there are a few drawbacks. For instance, it usually takes an expert or really dedicated user to make a Spore creature look like a real-world creature. (To see what it takes, you can find some interesting, but long, videos on YouTube about creating a dragon or Pokemon from Spore parts.)

We’re starting from a very different direction: our game is full of real world creatures like pigs, seagulls, weasels, etc, and things like long-extinct giant insects and dinosaurs… plus our starting blob of DNA (the Seed from the title). In short, mostly real creatures with very defined shapes. We think the results of using these parts are really satisfying in a way that’s quickly difficult to achieve with metaballs or similar systems. (Fans of E.V.O. will know what we’re talking about here.)

https://steamuserimages-a.akamaihd.net/ugc/2041867570345914997/88ABD5A5C4023A260E4ABDC0C690E5BD7B748D7E/

Animation is also a strength of our system. Like Spore we use inverse kinematic animations, but we do ours in a more traditional hand-animated way that results in an animation set PER creature, which can then be freely used on any other creature in the game (e.g. making a deer hop like a frog). Ultimately Spore had relatively few full animation sets; we’ll have dozens.

Hey, didn’t you guys make an evolution game before?
Yup. We made a 2D platformer called Miscreation that’s here on Steam. A lot of people really liked it. Unfortunately it was an early effort for our team and plagued by bugs. 

Our big mistake with Miscreation was developing the entire game and dropping it on Steam with only internal bug testing and feedback. 

With Strange Seed we’re going to release a demo as early as possible, and get as much of the game into people’s hands to play with and test as possible, a LONG time before release. If you want to help as a front-line tester please drop us a message!

When will Strange Seed be out?
Not for a while! We began in Jan-Feb 2023 and spent a while just nailing down the evolve system. Then we started on combat, UIs, some world building… but even a lot of what is currently on our Steam page is not final.

We’ll probably be able to release around mid-2024. As for an initial demo, we’re aiming for Fall 2023.

Got a roadmap?
Here’s a summary of what we’re working on in the next 2 months:

 Combat system improvements and polish
 Aesthetics: live-swapping skins and animation sets
 Part upgrade mini-game (the lab mechanic)
 Creature construction polish


We’ll keep posting updates on at least a monthly basis with where we are on the roadmap and what’s next.

This was too long!
I know, I’m sorry, this game is my life right now so I’m a bit obsessive. Thanks for making it to the end!
